Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

Scope: andesim qemu_plugin/ and runtime/. Find legacy: dead code in hybrid_handoff.c and other plugin sources (unused plugin args, code for the removed QEMU2 leg), libhotloops.so — check whether anything still uses it (grep both repos + docs), runtime/ sources superseded or unreferenced, Makefile cruft.

1	# Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
2	#
3	#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
4	#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
5	#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
6	#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
7	#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
8	#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
9	#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
10	#
11	# Users link with:
12	#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
13	# or, without the gcc driver:
14	#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
15	#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
16	#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
17	#
18	# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
19	# tests/fixtures/Makefile.
20	
21	# ARCH selects the target width: rv64 (default) or rv32. Each arch has its own
22	# toolchain (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32), triple, -march/-mabi, and
23	# output dir. rv64 stays at build/runtime (back-compat with `-B build/runtime`);
24	# rv32 lands at build/runtime/rv32 (`-B build/runtime/rv32`).
25	ARCH ?= rv64
26	
27	ifeq ($(ARCH),rv64)
28	  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
29	  TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
30	  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d
31	  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime
32	else ifeq ($(ARCH),rv32)
33	  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
34	  TRIPLE    := riscv32-unknown-elf
35	  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d
36	  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime/rv32
37	else
38	  $(error ARCH must be rv64 or rv32, got '$(ARCH)')
39	endif
40	
41	ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
42	$(error No toolchain for ARCH=$(ARCH). Set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (rv64) / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (rv32) in config.env, `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
43	endif
44	
45	CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
46	AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar
47	
48	# rvNNgc objects link cleanly into rvNNgcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V arch
49	# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants of the arch.
50	CFLAGS := $(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall
51	
52	LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o
53	
54	.PHONY: all clean
55	
56	all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
57	     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

59	$(OUT):
60		mkdir -p $@
61	
62	$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
63		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
64	
65	$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
66		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
67	
68	$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h
69	
70	$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
71		$(AR) rcs $@ $^

73	$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
74		cp $< $@
75

77		cp $< $@

80	# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
81	$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
82		mkdir -p $(dir $@)
83		cp $< $@

86		rm -rf $(OUT)

content.content:
# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector

Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.

## Usage

```
scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
```

The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
for other targets.

### Options

| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `contrib/plugins/`. Build once:

```
ninja -C build contrib-plugins
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
to be rebuilt.

## How it detects a loop

For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
iterations.

This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
semantics.

Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.

/* Unified linker script for all hybrid test fixtures.

 * Load base: 0x00100000 (1 MiB into andes_ae350 DRAM).
 *
 * andes_ae350 memory map:
 *   DRAM : 0x00000000 .. 0x7FFFFFFF  (writable, executable)
 *   MROM : 0x80000000 .. 0x87FFFFFF  (read-only)
 *
 * Reserved scratch (below text, used by .S fixtures):
 *   0x00000004              rt_csr_survival mtvec test value
 *   0x00001000              semihost_exit.inc param block
 *   0x00002000              rt_all_gprs spill area
 *   0x00003000              rt_mem_loadstore / rt_unaligned_lh buffer
 *   0x00010000              rt_shared_mem 4 KB buffer
 *
 * Layout above 0x00100000:
 *   .text         pinned at 0x00100000 (entry _start)
 *   .rodata
 *   .data         _edata terminates .data
 *   .bss          _end   terminates .bss (crt0 zeros [.bss, _end))
 *   _stack        0x00700000 (used by crt0.S to init sp)
 *
 * V-register transport scratch (L26): NOT a fixed address any more. The driver
 * maps one 4 KiB page above --mem-size and parks the scratch there (the mmap's
 * top page, v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + --mem-size), so it sits just past the
 * program's RAM -- nothing in this script can collide with it. No reservation
 * needed here.
 *
 * .S fixtures with no .data/.bss leave those sections empty (zero cost).
 * C fixtures rely on _edata / _end / _stack.
 */

ENTRY(_start)

SECTIONS {
    . = 0x00100000;

    .text : {
        *(.text.init)
        *(.text*)
    }

    .rodata : {
        *(.rodata*)
        *(.srodata*)
    }

    .data : {
        *(.data*)
        *(.sdata*)
    }
    _edata = .;

    .bss : {
        *(.bss*)
        *(.sbss*)
        *(COMMON)
    }
    _end = .;

    /* _stack sits well below V_SCRATCH (0x00FF0000) with ~9 MiB headroom.
     * Override at link time with -Wl,--defsym,_stack=... if needed. */
    PROVIDE(_stack = 0x00700000);
}

/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */
